He played [[college basketball]] for the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]]. He is a frequent rebounder and shot-blocker, and is noted for his speed and a near 7'0" wingspan.{{cite web|last1=Chapman|first1=Rex|title=The 2014 NBA Draft Has Ballooned Into A Scary Number's Game For Many|url=http://irex3.com/2014/04/23/2014-nba-draft-ballooned-scary-numbers-game-many/|work=IREX-3.com|date=April 23, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140704064233/http://www.irex3.com/2014/04/23/2014-nba-draft-ballooned-scary-numbers-game-many/|archive-date=July 4, 2014}} He won a national championship with [[Brewster Academy]] in 2012 after achieving star status with his high school team. ==High school career== Sampson attended [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]] in [[Akron, Ohio]] from 2007 to 2010, before transferring to [[Brewster Academy]] in August 2010 for his senior year.{{cite web|last1=Rogers|first1=Tim|title=Basketball standout JaKarr Sampson leaves St. Vincent-St. Mary|url=http://highschoolsports.cleveland.com/news/article/-7823762485261239516/basketball-standout-jakarr-sampson-leaves-st-vincent-st-mary/|work=Cleveland.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|date=August 26, 2010}} In November 2010, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] at [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]].{{cite web|last1=Darcy|first1=Kieran|title=St. John's signs three top players|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/news/story?id=5788376|work=ESPN.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|date=November 10, 2010}} As a senior in 2010–11, Sampson averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.0 blocks per game, leading Brewster to a 31–3 record. He went on to be named to the All-NEPSAC first team.{{cite web|title=JaKarr Sampson Bio|url=http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jakarr_sampson_822299.html|work=RedStormSports.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|archive-date=July 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714212556/http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jakarr_sampson_822299.html|url-status=dead}} Following the 2010–11 season, Sampson was set to join the St. John's Red Storm in 2011–12 for his freshman season, but failed to qualify academically and was ineligible to attend college. Sampson subsequently returned to Brewster Academy for another season, and led Brewster to a prep national championship.{{cite web|last1=Darcy|first1=Kieran|title=Jakarr Sampson chooses St. John's|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/ncb/story/_/id/7689201/st-john-red-storm-land-prized-basketball-recruit-jakarr-sampson|work=ESPN.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|date=March 15, 2012}} In 2011–12, he averaged 18.5 points and 11.0 rebounds per game as he was named the NEPSAC AAA Player of the Year and Most Valuable Player of the National Prep Championship. In March 2012, Sampson recommitted to St. John's. ==College career== In his freshman season at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], Sampson was named the 2013 [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Big East Rookie of the Year]], and was also named to the Big East All-Rookie team.{{cite web|last1=Leach|first1=Jason|title=St John's JaKarr Sampson named Big East Rookie of the Year|url=http://theharlemtimes.com/sports/st-johns-jakarr-sampson-named-big-east-rookie-of-the-year|work=TheHarlemTimes.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|date=March 13, 2013}} In 33 games, he averaged 14.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks in 31.5 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=JaKarr Sampson Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jakarr-sampson-1.html |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=June 26, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702201135/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jakarr-sampson-1.html |archive-date=July 2, 2014 }} In his sophomore season, he recorded 424 points and 202 rebounds, completing his Red Storm career with totals of 915 points and 420 rebounds. He was named to the 2013 Pre-season All-Big East second team. In 33 games, he averaged 12.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.0 blocks in 29.0 minutes per game. On March 24, 2014, Sampson announced his intentions to enter the 2014 NBA draft and forgo his final two years of college eligibility.{{cite web|title=St. John's JaKarr Sampson Announces Intentions To Enter NBA Draft|url=http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032414aab.html|work=RedStormSports.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|date=March 24, 2014|archive-date=July 14, ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2014–2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Sampson joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Sixers Announce Orlando Pro Summer League Camp Invitees|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140701-opsl-camp-invitees|access-date=July 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2014}} On September 29, 2014, he signed with the 76ers.{{cite news|title=Sixers Announce 2014 Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140929-camp-roster|access-date=September 29, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2014}} On November 21, Sampson was assigned to the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]], the 76ers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.{{cite news|title=Sixers Assign JaKarr Sampson To Delaware 87ers|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141121-sampson-assigned|access-date=November 21, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2014}} Three days later, he was recalled by the 76ers.{{cite news|title=Sixers Recall JaKarr Sampson From Delaware 87ers|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141124-sampson-recall|access-date=November 24, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2014}} Sampson made 74 appearances (including 32 starts) for Philadelphia during his rookie campaign, averaging 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.0 assist.{{Cite web|title=Ja’Karr Sampson 2014-15 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2608891/type/nba/year/2015|access-date=August 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Sampson made 47 appearances (including 18 starts) for the 76ers during the [[2015–16 NBA season]], recording averages of 5.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Ja’Karr Sampson 2015-16 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2608891/type/nba/year/2016|access-date=August 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On February 18, 2016, Sampson was waived by the team.{{cite news|title=Sixers Acquire 2017 Second Round Pick, Joel Anthony|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-acquire-2017-second-round-pick-joel-anthony|access-date=February 18, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2016}} ===Denver Nuggets (2016)=== On February 22, 2016, Sampson signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite news|title=Nuggets Sign JaKarr Sampson|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-jakarr-sampson|access-date=February 22, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut with the Nuggets in a 114–110 loss to the [[2015–16 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]], recording one rebound and one steal in fourteen minutes off the bench.{{cite news|title=Cousins helps Kings hold off Nuggets for 114-110 win|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160223/SACDEN/gameinfo.html|access-date=February 24, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2016}} Sampson made 26 appearances (22 starts) for Denver, logging averages of 5.2 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. On October 15, Sampson was waived by the Nuggets.{{cite web|author=NuggetsPR|url=https://twitter.com/NuggetsPR/status/787324175207702528|title=#Nuggets Waive Kennedy, Sampson and...|work=Twitter|date=October 15, 2016|access-date=October 15, 2016}} ===Iowa Energy (2016–2017)=== On October 21, 2016, Sampson signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],{{cite news|title=Grizzlies sign JaKarr Sampson|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jakarr-sampson-signed-161021|access-date=October 21, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2016}} but was waived the next day.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/sampson-selden-stephens-waived-161022|title=Grizzlies waive JaKarr Sampson, Wayne Selden Jr. & D.J. Stephens|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}} Seven days later, he was acquired by the [[Iowa Wolves|Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://iowa.dleague.nba.com/news/energy-announce-returning-affiliate-tryout-players-2/|title=Energy Announce Returning, Affiliate and Tryout Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016|archive-date=February 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216050317/http://iowa.dleague.nba.com/news/energy-announce-returning-affiliate-tryout-players-2/|url-status=dead}} On February 6, 2017, he was named in the Western Conference All-Star team for the 2017 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Rosters for 2017 NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 7, 2017}} ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2018)=== On July 29, 2017, Sampson was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the NBA. Under the terms of the deal, for the 2017–18 season, he will have a one-year deal splitting time between the Kings and their G-League affiliate, the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]]. On December 6, Sampson grabbed a career-high 16 rebounds in a loss to the [[2017–18 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite news|title=Kings Sign JaKarr Sampson to Two-Way Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-jakarr-sampson-two-way-contract|access-date=July 29, 2017|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 29, 2017}} Sampson played 35 games with the Bighorns and averaged 17.9 points, 7.1 rebounds and 1.06 steals per game.{{cite web |title=Bulls Finalize Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-finalize-training-camp-roster-2 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 24, 2018 |date=September 24, 2018}} In 22 appearances (six starts) for Sacramento in the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]], he recorded averages of 4.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 0.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Ja’Karr Sampson 2017-18 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2608891/type/nba/year/2018|access-date=August 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Windy City Bulls (2018)=== On September 24, 2018, Sampson signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] for training camp. He was waived by the Bulls on October 12.{{cite web |title=Bulls waive four players|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-four-players|website=NBA.com |access-date=October 16, 2018 |date=October 12, 2018}} On October 20, the [[Windy City Bulls]] announced that they had acquired the returning rights to Sampson Johnson and the No. 38 overall pick in the [[2018 NBA G League Draft]], Mike Amius from [[Iowa Wolves]] for the returning rights to [[Jarell Eddie]] and [[Jaylen Johnson]],{{cite web|first1=Kalyn|last1=Hutchinson|title=WINDY CITY SELECTS TWO PLAYERS IN NBA G LEAGUE DRAFT; ACQUIRE MIKE AMIUS AND RIGHTS TO JAKARR SAMPSON|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-selects-two-players-in-nba-g-league-draft-acquire-mike-amius-and-rights-to-jakarr-sampson/|date=October 20, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 20, 2018}} and later on November 9, the [[Windy City Bulls]] acquired Sampson.{{cite web|title=WINDY CITY BULLS ACQUIRE JAKARR SAMPSON|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-acquire-jakarr-sampson/|date=November 9, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 9, 2018}} ===Shandong Golden Stars (2018–2019)===
